configKeys.effect: List of custom SHAPED recipes in the format recipe_id;result_item;result_count;pattern;keys (pattern as AAA|BBB|AAA or "AAA" "BBB" "AAA"; keys as A=minecraft:green_wool,B=minecraft:chest; ingredients may be tags with a leading #). A recipe_id that matches an existing recipe replaces it.
configKeys.range: no spec range; per-entry validator requires 5 semicolon-separated parts, two parsable ResourceLocations and result_count 1-64

configKeys.effect: List of custom SHAPELESS recipes in the format ingredient1,ingredient2,...->result_item[;result_count[;recipe_id]], with item IDs or #tags as ingredients. Omitting recipe_id auto-generates minecraft:shapeless_<result path>.
configKeys.range: no spec range; per-entry validator requires an -> arrow, a non-empty ingredient part, a parsable result ResourceLocation and, if given, result_count 1-64 and a parsable recipe_id

events: net.neoforged.neoforge.event.AddReloadListenerEvent (CustomCraftingRecipesModule.java:62-69, @SubscribeEvent on the instance registered to NeoForge.EVENT_BUS in onInitialize, line 54-56; body returns immediately unless isModuleEnabled()) - the module's only event handler
notes:
DOC-WRITER NOTES (each point re-verified against the current working tree; line numbers are from it).

1. STALE TODO CONTRADICTS THE DOCS AND CLAUDE.md. CustomCraftingRecipesModule.java:58-61 carries a block comment: "TODO: Migrate from code-injected recipes to proper JSON datapack recipes (data/<ns>/recipe/*.json - singular folder since MC 1.21). This RecipeManager injection is a workaround because the old plural recipes/ folder never loaded. See docs/custom_crafting_recipes.md ("TODO / Roadmap") for the correct format." That contradicts docs/modules/custom_crafting_recipes.md, which ends its convention section with "This is intentional and final - there is no plan to migrate to JSON datapacks", and the repo CLAUDE.md ("Keine Migration zu JSON geplant"). The referenced "TODO / Roadmap" section does not exist in the doc any more (the doc's sections are Overview / Shaped recipes / Shapeless recipes / Behaviour notes / Convention / See also). Treat the TODO as dead text, not as roadmap.

2. HOW IT WORKS. onInitialize (line 54-56) does nothing but NeoForge.EVENT_BUS.register(this). On AddReloadListenerEvent (line 62-69, gated by isModuleEnabled()) it adds an inner PreparableReloadListener named "vanillaplusadditions_custom_crafting_recipes" (line 251-273) holding the RecipeManager from event.getServerResources().getRecipeManager(). On reload it waits on the preparation barrier and then, on the game executor, merges its parsed recipes into a LinkedHashMap keyed by RecipeHolder.id() seeded from recipeManager.getRecipes(), and calls recipeManager.replaceRecipes(mergedRecipes.values()) (line 80-96). It then logs INFO "Applied {} custom recipes ({} added, {} replaced)." (line 97-98). Effect: a config recipe whose id equals an existing recipe id REPLACES it; any other id is added. This is the same pattern a dozen other modules in this repo use (grep replaceRecipes: flying_fish, cat_guardian, battle_dogs, axolotl_guardian, end_conduit, minecart_chunk_loading, ...).

3. ID COLLISION IS THE DESIGNED OVERRIDE MECHANISM. The default entry "minecraft:netherite_ingot;..." deliberately reuses the vanilla recipe id and therefore drops vanilla's shapeless scrap+gold recipe in favour of a shaped one. Documented in the CustomCraftingRecipesConfig comment above NETHERITE_INGOT_FROM_POWDERED_OBSIDIAN (config lines 35-37) and in the module doc.

4. PRECISION ON THE NETHERITE RECIPE. The replacement does NOT remove gold entirely: pattern PSP|SGS|PSP means 4x create:powdered_obsidian (corners), 4x minecraft:netherite_scrap (edges) and 1x minecraft:gold_ingot (centre) -> 1 netherite ingot. So it trades most of the gold for Powdered Obsidian, one ingot stays. Do not write "instead of gold" without that qualification.

5. MISSING-MOD HANDLING IS IMPLICIT, NOT A ModList GATE ON THE MODULE. unknownItem()/isModAbsent() (line 219-233) turn an unknown ITEM id into a MissingModException when its namespace is neither "minecraft" nor "neoforge" and ModList.get().isLoaded(namespace) is false. Such entries are dropped with a logger.debug line per entry plus one summary INFO "Skipped custom crafting recipes for mods that are not installed: <namespaces>" (line 157-160). A wrong id whose mod IS installed raises a plain IllegalArgumentException and is logged at ERROR instead (line 126-127 / 150-151). So Create/Overpacked recipes go inert with only a DEBUG line and one INFO summary; the module itself stays active and the other entries still load. There is no shouldInitialize() override anywhere in the module, hence requiredMods is empty.

6. THE MOD GATE ONLY COVERS ITEM IDS, NOT TAGS. ingredientFromString (line 198-211) resolves a "#..."-prefixed ingredient straight into Ingredient.of(TagKey.create(Registries.ITEM, ...)) without ever touching BuiltInRegistries or isModAbsent. A tag ingredient naming an absent mod's tag is therefore NOT skipped as a missing-mod recipe - the recipe is still registered, with whatever that tag resolves to. Only item ids (result item and non-tag ingredients) are mod-gated.

7. "minecraft:air" IS REJECTED, NOT ACCEPTED. Both createShapedRecipe/createShapelessRecipe and ingredientFromString compare the looked-up Item against Items.AIR to detect an unknown id (lines 167, 184, 206). Since BuiltInRegistries.ITEM.get(minecraft:air) legitimately returns AIR, an explicit minecraft:air is reported as "Unknown result item: minecraft:air" / "Unknown ingredient item: ..." and the entry is dropped with an ERROR. Empty grid cells are written as spaces in the pattern instead (the doc says so).

8. THE TWO "SAMPLE" DEFAULTS ARE REAL, SHIPPED RECIPES, not inert examples. SAMPLE_RECIPE crafts 1x overpacked:giant_backpack from 5x leather, 2x string, 1x create:andesite_alloy and 1x create:item_vault under the id vanillaplusadditions:giant_backpack - it needs BOTH Overpacked (result) and Create (ingredients) and is skipped if either is missing. SAMPLE_SHAPELESS_RECIPE adds leather+string -> 1 bundle under the auto-generated id minecraft:shapeless_bundle, i.e. it does not reuse vanilla's minecraft:bundle id and is therefore additive, not a replacement. Neither the README paragraph (README.md:123-124) nor the module doc mentions that the bundle or the backpack recipe ships enabled - the README only names the rail upgrades and the netherite rework.

9. ALL RECIPES LAND IN CraftingBookCategory.MISC with an empty group ("") - shaped (line 178) and shapeless (line 194) alike. No recipe-book grouping, no per-recipe category control.

10. PARSING QUIRKS worth documenting. Shaped pattern rows are taken from quoted segments first via the regex "([^"]+)" (QUOTED_PATTERN, line 44, used at 310-317); only if no quoted row is found does it split on "|", or on "," when no "|" is present (line 319-321) - so a comma-separated pattern works, undocumented. Those splits use the zero-limit String.split, so trailing empty rows are dropped. A key symbol must be exactly one character and must not be a space (line 340-348). result_count is validated 1..64 twice: in the ModConfigSpec validator and again at parse time (config 92-95 / 117-120, module 291-293 / 396-398). The shapeless recipe_id, when omitted, defaults to ResourceLocation.withDefaultNamespace("shapeless_" + result path) (line 391/393), so auto-generated ids always land in the MINECRAFT namespace, never in vanillaplusadditions.

11. CONFIG VALIDATOR IS SHALLOW. isValidShapedRecipeEntry only checks the 5 parts, the two ResourceLocations, the count range and that pattern/keys are non-empty; isValidShapelessRecipeEntry checks the arrow, a non-empty ingredient part, the result ResourceLocation and (if present) count range and recipe id. A syntactically plausible but semantically broken entry passes the validator and is rejected at parse time with an ERROR log, while the rest of the list still loads. What happens to a list containing an entry the validator REJECTS (single element corrected vs. whole list reset to the defaults) is NeoForge ModConfigSpec behaviour and is not provable from this repository - do not state it in the doc.

12. THE "DEAD CODE" IN ShapelessRecipeDefinition.parse IS HALF ALIVE. "if (resultParts.length < 1)" (line 378) really is unreachable: String.split never returns a zero-length array here, because resultPart is split with limit 2 and even "" yields one element (verified). BUT "if (ingredients.isEmpty())" (line 405) IS reachable: Java's zero-limit String.split drops trailing empty strings, so ",".split(",") and " , ".trim().split(",") both return a ZERO-length array (verified by running it on this machine's JDK). An entry like ",->minecraft:bundle" passes the config validator (its ingredient part "," is non-empty) and then hits exactly that guard, which throws "At least one ingredient is required" and is logged at ERROR. The same mechanism keeps the shaped guards live: a keys part of "," produces an empty key map ("keys must define at least one symbol") and a pattern part of "," produces no rows ("pattern must define at least one row").

13. DUPLICATE IDS. seenRecipeIds is shared across the shaped and the shapeless pass (line 103, used at 114 and 139), so a shapeless entry can override a shaped one with the same id. It is not silent: the code logs WARN "Duplicate custom recipe id in config. Last one wins: {}" and removes the earlier holder from the parsed list (line 115-118 / 140-143).

14. THE DOC'S DEBUG-LOGGING SENTENCE IS INACCURATE. docs/modules/custom_crafting_recipes.md says "Enable debug logging for this module to see every recipe that gets loaded" - there is no per-recipe "loaded" log at all. The only shouldDebugLog()-gated line is "No custom crafting recipes configured." (line 74-76). The per-entry skip lines (123-124, 147-148) are plain getLogger().debug(...) calls on a bare SLF4J logger (AbstractModule line 38/60-62), so they depend on the log level, not on the module's debug_logging config key.

15. NO ASSETS OF ANY KIND. No lang keys (grep -i "crafting" in assets/vanillaplusadditions/lang/en_us.json returns nothing - all log output is hardcoded English, there is no player-facing text at all). No mixins (no mixin/custom_crafting_recipes package; no entry in vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json). No DeferredRegister, hence no items/blocks/entities. No commands, no keybinds. The build.gradle standalone entry (line 418) is the bare two-field form with no dataGlobs, no moduleDeps and no mixins.

16. PACKAGING. Bundle: VanillaPlusAdditions.java:164, unconditional moduleManager.registerModule(new CustomCraftingRecipesModule()). Standalone: standalone/custom_crafting_recipes/CustomCraftingRecipesStandalone.java, @Mod("vpa_custom_crafting_recipes"), booted via StandaloneModuleBootstrap; build.gradle:418 lists it as 'Vanilla Plus: Custom Crafting Recipes'.

17. README/doc path drift (currently uncommitted docs reorg): README.md:300 still links docs/custom_crafting_recipes.md while git status shows the staged rename to docs/modules/custom_crafting_recipes.md. The module-source TODO comment (line 61) points at the old path too. docs/modules/pathfinder_quills.md:62 and CLAUDE.md:94 also still use the old path.

18. UNRESOLVED: whether the replaced recipe set reaches already-connected clients. replaceRecipes runs server-side inside the reload listener; the repo contains no ClientboundUpdateRecipesPacket or any other recipe-sync code for this module, so client sync relies entirely on vanilla/NeoForge reload behaviour. Not provable from this repository - do not claim either way in the docs.
oneLiner: Lets you write extra crafting recipes straight into the config file instead of a datapack - and ships a few by default: plain rails upgrade into powered/detector/activator rails, leather plus string makes a bundle, and (with Create installed) the Netherite Ingot is crafted from scrap and Powdered Obsidian with just one gold ingot left in the middle.

optionalMods.whatItAdds: Two of the five default shaped recipes need Create items: the Netherite Ingot rework (create:powdered_obsidian) and the Giant Backpack recipe (create:item_vault, create:andesite_alloy). Without Create both entries are dropped with a DEBUG line each plus one INFO summary, so vanilla's original scrap+gold Netherite recipe stays in place and the backpack recipe simply does not exist. The module itself still runs and the remaining entries still load.

Supplies the result item of the default SAMPLE_RECIPE (overpacked:giant_backpack). Without Overpacked that one entry is dropped the same way (the result item is resolved first, so 'overpacked' is the namespace reported); nothing else is lost.

recipes: SHAPED vanillaplusadditions:giant_backpack -> 1x overpacked:giant_backpack; pattern CDC|ABA|AAA with A=minecraft:leather, B=create:item_vault, C=minecraft:string, D=create:andesite_alloy (= 5x leather, 2x string, 1x item vault, 1x andesite alloy). Needs Overpacked AND Create; skipped otherwise. Shipped as a default, though neither README nor doc mentions it.

SHAPED vanillaplusadditions:powered_rail_from_rails -> 6x minecraft:powered_rail; pattern 'R R|RGR|RDR' with R=minecraft:rail, G=minecraft:gold_ingot, D=minecraft:redstone (= 6x rail, 1x gold ingot, 1x redstone). Fair rail upgrade, additive - the vanilla recipe id is untouched.

SHAPED vanillaplusadditions:detector_rail_from_rails -> 6x minecraft:detector_rail; pattern 'R R|RPR|RDR' with R=minecraft:rail, P=minecraft:stone_pressure_plate, D=minecraft:redstone (= 6x rail, 1x stone pressure plate, 1x redstone). Additive.

SHAPED vanillaplusadditions:activator_rail_from_rails -> 6x minecraft:activator_rail; pattern RSR|RTR|RSR with R=minecraft:rail, S=minecraft:stick, T=minecraft:redstone_torch (= 6x rail, 2x stick, 1x redstone torch). Additive.

SHAPED minecraft:netherite_ingot -> 1x minecraft:netherite_ingot; pattern PSP|SGS|PSP with P=create:powdered_obsidian, S=minecraft:netherite_scrap, G=minecraft:gold_ingot (= 4x powdered obsidian in the corners, 4x netherite scrap on the edges, 1x gold ingot in the centre). Reuses the VANILLA recipe id, so it REPLACES vanilla's shapeless scrap+gold recipe. Inert without Create, in which case the vanilla recipe survives untouched.

SHAPELESS minecraft:leather + minecraft:string -> 1x minecraft:bundle, auto-generated id minecraft:shapeless_bundle (does not reuse vanilla's minecraft:bundle id, so it is additive). Shipped as a default, not mentioned in README or doc.
Plus: anything the user adds to the 'recipes' / 'shapeless_recipes' config lists - that is the module's actual purpose.
shortDescription: Adds configurable shaped crafting recipes from the module config.
